Eden (Customer): Hey team — hitting an error when trying to stream responses from the /v1/rerank endpoint. Customer expected a chunked stream of scores but keeps getting a 415/unsupported media type. Posting the curl we used:

Eden (Customer): ```bash
curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  -d '{"query":"best intro lines","candidates":["line A","line B","line C"]}'
```

Eden (Customer): Response: 415 Unsupported Media Type, body: "rerank endpoint does not support streaming"

Eden (Customer): This used to work? At least our UX expects incremental scores as they arrive so we switched to streaming everywhere. Any quick workaround?

Alex (Support): @Eden thanks for the details — sorry for the friction. Quick Qs: are you trying to use server-sent events (SSE) or just chunked JSON arrays? And can you paste full raw headers from the request/response if available?

Eden (Customer): We're using SSE. We have a node client that sets `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and uses `fetch` with `body` streaming. Headers from response: `HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type`, `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, body `{ "error": "streaming not supported on rerank" }`

Alex (Support): Got it. This aligns with what I expect: rerank is currently a synchronous endpoint — clients must send a normal JSON POST (application/json) and receive a single JSON response with scores. Streaming is supported for generation/chat endpoints only.

Alex (Support): Repro steps I ran locally:
```
# failing (streaming headers)
curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' \n  -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["a","b"]}'
# returns 415 and body with message indicating streaming unsupported

# working (sync)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["a","b"]}'
# returns 200 JSON: {"scores":[0.78,0.22],"candidate_ids":[...]}
```

Shreya (ML Eng): adding context — rerank runs a lightweight scoring pass over candidates, returns full ranking and scores in one shot. We don't maintain an SSE stream or token-level generation. If someone attempts to use streaming headers the router returns 415 because the runtime can't upgrade the connection to a stream for this path.

Shreya (ML Eng): Also note: we validate payload shape on entry. If you accidentally send an NDJSON stream or chunked JSON pieces the server may respond with 400 or an early parse error. Best to send a single application/json body.

Eden (Customer): Okay helpful. The product UX relies on incremental updates — is there any recommended pattern? Could we poll the rerank endpoint or switch to a generation endpoint to compute scores incrementally?

Matt (DevEx): Polling is the simplest: call rerank with smaller candidate batches and stream progress in your UI. Alternatively, if you need token-level streaming for a reranking-like process, one pattern is to use the generation API to compute signals as partial outputs become available, then hit rerank synchronously for final aggregation. Both have tradeoffs on cost/latency.

Alex (Support): For immediate fix, please change your client to set `Content-Type: application/json` and send the full payload in one POST. Example minimal repro that should work for you right now: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"best intro lines","candidates":["line A","line B","line C"]}'
```

Alex (Support): We'll also include a clear error message and docs note so folks understand rerank is synchronous. Shreya — can we make the router return a more actionable 415 body like `{error: "rerank does not support streaming. use application/json POST or use /v1/generate for streams"}`? Right now the message is terse and customers are confused.

Shreya (ML Eng): Yep — I can add a small change to check request.headers.accept/content-type on the routing layer and return that improved diagnostics. I'll file an infra PR and target a patch for this week.

Alex (Support): Thanks. I'll send Eden a temporary reply to unblock them and include a short code snippet + recovery steps. Also I'll add a KB entry.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-4521 created for this customer issue and assigned to eng-runtime.

Eden (Customer): Thanks all. One last Q: we sometimes get weird score ranges on rerank (negatives or >1). Could that be related to model mismatch or streaming attempts?

Shreya (ML Eng): Unrelated to streaming — rerank returns whatever scoring function the model provides. Most of our verified model variants output normalized [0,1] scores, but third-party or custom scoring heads could be unnormalized. If you're seeing unexpected ranges, include the model name/variant and an example payload and we'll inspect. Also ensure you don't accidentally parse the body as a newline-delimited stream which could produce partial numbers.

Alex (Support): For Eden: follow-up actions from us: 1) temporary mitigation: switch to application/json POST and poll smaller batches; 2) Shreya will add clearer 415 error wording; 3) Matt will add a KB snippet to support docs explaining rerank vs generate streaming semantics; 4) we'll keep this ticket open until you're unblocked.

Eden (Customer): Great — switching client now and will report back if we hit anything else. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

Alex (Support): Closing loop here once you confirm. If you want, paste a snippet of your client code (node/ts) and we can suggest an exact tiny change.

Eden (Customer): Will do. Thanks!
